usage: dotkit <command> [options]

Day-to-day commands for a Mac with dotkit. Run them from any directory.

Apply and update the config:
  apply      Apply the config: Nix, Homebrew, and mise.
  upgrade    Get new releases. Shows one plan, asks once, then applies.

Tools in the lists:
  add        Select the source for a tool, add it, and apply.
  remove     Remove a tool from the config that declares it, and apply.
  info       Where a tool is declared, its command, and its sources.
  list       The declared tools.

Check:
  doctor     What your dotfiles repeat or replace of the dotkit base.
  history    The package changes of the last apply.

Bring this Mac under dotkit:
  migrate    Add the tools that were installed by hand to the lists.
  tidy       Give the apps of this Mac a clean source, and remove old copies.

Recovery and cleanup:
  rollback   Go back to the previous Nix generation.
  clean      Delete old Nix generations, Homebrew downloads, and mise versions.

Run `dotkit <command> --help` for the options of a command.

Examples:
  dotkit add lazygit          Nix, mise, or Homebrew: dotkit add selects one
  dotkit add npm:cowsay       A prefix selects the source (dotkit add --help)
  dotkit upgrade -n           Show what is outdated
  dotkit upgrade mise         Upgrade only the mise tools
  DOTKIT_DIR=~/.dotkit dotkit apply
                              Use a dotkit checkout instead of the locked release

New Mac: see the dotkit README.
